`aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng` already depends on `aws_iam_role.managed_ng` via `node_role_arn = ... aws_iam_role.managed_ng[0].arn`. Listing `aws_iam_role.managed_ng` in `depends_on` duplicates that implicit reference.

`null_resource.update_trust_policy` already depends on `aws_iam_role.emr_on_eks_execution` because its `local-exec` command interpolates `${aws_iam_role.emr_on_eks_execution.id}`. The `depends_on` entry is redundant.

`null_resource.update_trust_policy` already depends on `kubernetes_namespace.spark` because its `local-exec` command interpolates `${kubernetes_namespace.spark.id}`. The `depends_on` entry is redundant.

`kubernetes_storage_class_v1.gp3` advertises provisioner `ebs.csi.aws.com`, but the self-managed EBS CSI driver is installed by `module.aws_ebs_csi_driver` (enabled via `enable_self_managed_aws_ebs_csi_driver = true`). The StorageClass has no dependency on that driver install, so it can be created before the driver exists. No clean attribute reference exists to wire this, so an explicit `depends_on` is needed.

`kubernetes_storage_class_v1.efs` advertises provisioner `efs.csi.aws.com`, but the EFS CSI driver is installed by `module.aws_efs_csi_driver` (enabled via `enable_aws_efs_csi_driver = true`). The StorageClass depends on the EFS filesystem (`module.efs`) but not on the driver install, so ordering between the driver and the StorageClass is not guaranteed. No clean attribute reference exists to wire this, so an explicit `depends_on` is needed.
